payload.analysis_method: Read the immutable execution state, original plan/review, reviewed retrospective plan/review, sealed prior analysis and its manifest, the two bound reference CSVs, the sealed 60-unit morphology JSON, metrics CSV, decision CSV, and prior analysis source. No solver, fitting unit, curve-score call, or curve-diagnostic call was run. A bounded native audit reapplied the reviewed M0-M2/S0-S2 row masks and each of the four global x/y sign corners directly to the reference rows. It counted y<=0/nonfinite rows and non-strict transformed x for consecutive point_index pairs, without sorting, deleting rows, bridging gaps, changing weights, or fitting. Its 48 issue labels were compared with the sealed unit ledger and had zero mismatches. Curve tooling was unnecessary because the unresolved quantity is a pre-fit corner qualification failure rather than a local residual question.

hypothesis_assessments.rationale: The central own-anchor constant-D family differs strongly from the reference morphology, but digitization-range compatibility is unavailable and the existing material/D pairings do not isolate surface-boundary control. A high simulated tail persists across central support masks with very small numerical sensitivity, but shared/detection-limited support and a valid joint digitization range are unresolved. Nonpositive y-minus rows in S masks and non-strict transformed x prevent the required compatibility test, so neither support nor contradiction is licensed.

objective_assessment.summary: The three retrospective morphology objectives have supported central and mask-sensitivity values and explicit material-specific limits. Their required digitization ranges and compatibility classifications remain not evaluable under the reviewed global-corner construction, and the later mechanism-separation objective remains uncovered.

payload.remaining_contradiction: For both materials, the sealed central and mask-specific reductions consistently show that the frozen constant-D own-anchor curves have later operational endpoints, wider transitions, and substantially higher tail-center levels than the bound reference. Numerical tightening changes these reported quantities negligibly. Yet every preregistered global digitization corner violates a qualification rule before fitting: variable per-row x uncertainty creates non-strict consecutive positions in 38 corners, and y-minus creates a nonpositive value in 10 S-mask corners. Consequently no min-max digitization range, compatible/outside classification, uncertainty-qualified shape comparison, or platform consistency conclusion is available. This is a limitation of the supplied marginal uncertainties combined with the reviewed global-corner construction; it is not an unfinished batch or fitting failure. Even after an uncertainty revision, the current material/D confounding and absence of a finite shape-changing structural counterfactual would still prevent kick-out, VCD, or unique material-mechanism identification. The external execution also remains independently failed/97.
payload.summary: This continuation diagnoses the uncertainty boundary of the sealed retrospective Fig. 4 morphology analysis without rerunning its 60 fitting units or any solver. The completed central reductions support material-specific descriptive morphology: for M0, the own-anchor operational endpoint b2 is 0.618317 versus 0.474752 um for In0.83Al0.17As and 0.535149 versus 0.387624 um for In0.83Ga0.17As; transition widths are 0.176238 versus 0.054455 um and 0.262376 versus 0.053465 um. The own-anchor tail-center excess is 3.04143 and 2.54056 decades, respectively. Across M0-M2/S0-S2, own-anchor b2 spans 0.554950-0.618317 um for InAlAs and 0.535149-0.536139 um for InGaAs, while width spans 0.167327-0.226733 and 0.259406-0.262376 um. All position/width primary-minus-tight differences are zero, and the largest absolute slope/level difference is below 1.75e-5, although no reviewed threshold turns this into a convergence claim. Front and tail candidate regions meet the minimum support rule, but their physical plateau status and digitization-range consistency remain unqualified. The independent audit exactly reproduced the sealed corner ledger: all 48 global corners fail before fitting, with 38 non-strict-x failures and 10 y-minus nonpositive failures. Variable per-row x uncertainties make a common sign shift tie or reverse many consecutive point_index pairs; S masks omit the y>y_uncertainty requirement and therefore admit rows whose y-minus corner is nonpositive. The implementation follows the reviewed rules by failing closed, so the missing ranges are caused by the supplied marginal uncertainty plus the global-corner contract, not by QR fitting, interpolation, numerical sensitivity, or the constant-D scientific model. Separately, the immutable external execution remains failed/97 because of the declared TDR-path mismatch, and the available material/D pairings plus absence of shape-changing structural counterfactuals still prevent microscopic mechanism identification.
